title: Harmonize chroma hierarchy and fluid type scale for core primitives
creator: Sofia Liao
description:
Goal: Define a compact, hierarchical chroma system and a fluid typographic rhythm that scales predictably across component primitives (buttons, tables, charts) to reduce token surface area while improving accessibility and composability.

Scope:
- Color: establish 6-level chroma scales for semantic roles (accent, neutral, success, warning, danger, surface) with clear token naming and aliasing rules.
- Typography: introduce a fluid type scale (px + relative tokens) with 3 density presets (compact, default, spacious) and a named rhythm for headlines, labels, body, and microcopy.
- Spacing & radius: re-evaluate base spacing unit and radius tokens to align with new type rhythm; introduce proportional radii for primitives.
- Elevation & shadow: simplify elevation steps to 3 pragmatic stops optimized for high-contrast and low-contrast themes; encode shadow as tokenized combos (ambient + key).

Why now: The current token set has accumulated redundant hues and micro-variants across components, causing inconsistent rendering in low-density contexts and divergent developer usage. Standardizing chroma hierarchy and a fluid type rhythm reduces decision surface for engineers and makes rollout to Dedicated/Private deployments easier.

Deliverables:
- Token spec doc with explicit color values, contrast ratios, and migration mapping from old tokens to new tokens.
- Figma library files containing updated tokens and component examples in three densities.
- Engineering token migration guide (one-page) and codemod suggestions.
- QA checklist and accessibility report demonstrating contrast coverage for AA/AAA where applicable.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- We prioritize AA contrast for body text and interactive controls; some decorative accents will be allowed at lower contrast with documentation.
- Reducing token count may require aliasing; we will favor semantic tokens over presentational tokens to preserve flexibility.
- Fluid type adds complexity to mobile breakpoints; we propose fixed breakpoints for mobile vs desktop to keep runtime calculations simple.

Rollout plan:
1) Lock final palette and type scale in design and publish to Figma (Week 1).
2) Create engineering tokens and pull request with mapping and examples (Week 2).
3) Small-batch rollout to low-risk UI (internal tools) and iterate (Week 3).
4) Full rollout with migration scripts and feature flags for public dashboards (Week 4).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Token spec document published with unambiguous values, naming conventions, and migration table to existing tokens
A2: All core interactive components (primary/secondary button, table row, chart axis/legend) have design variants implemented in Figma for compact/default/spacious densities
A3: Accessibility report shows body text and primary actions meet WCAG AA contrast in default and high-contrast themes
A4: Engineering PR created that adds new token set and includes at least one example app page converted to new tokens
A5: Migration guidance and codemod examples are available in the repo and reviewed by eng leads
A6: Rollout plan documented with feature-flag gating and rollback steps
